Big Question
Today’s Wonder

Ralph blows a shell and a crowd becomes a meeting. What turns a scattered crowd into a group?

🎯
Objectives
By the end of this lesson…
🐚Craft: I will name a symbol and say what the conch stands for so far.
🧭Reading: I will map the island from Chapter 1 and explain what two moments, side by side, suggest about the boys and the island.
🔤Words: I will learn five words from Chapter 1.
🪶Poem: I will listen to the opening of Yeats’s “The Second Coming” and mark one line.
✏️Writing: I will punctuate a line of dialogue, retell a chapter in order, and copy a passage exactly, then say what one mark in it does.

🪶 Poetry Corner
The Second Coming
by W. B. Yeats (1920)
Lines 1–4 of 22
0:16 AI voice
🖋️ PenTap the line that says the middle can no longer keep things together.
Turning and turning in the widening gyre The falcon cannot hear the falconer; Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold; Mere anarchy is loosed upon the world,
gyre: a spiral, a widening circle · falconer: a person who trains and flies a hunting falcon · centre: the British spelling of center; here, the middle that holds things together · anarchy: a state with no ruler and no order · loosed: let loose, set free
Photograph: George Charles Beresford, 1911, public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

🎓 Questions from Professor Lovelore

Professor Lovelore
First question. Piggy asks Ralph not to tell the others his nickname. Then, in front of everyone, Ralph says it. What does that moment show about Ralph so far?
Your answer
Professor Lovelore
Next. Jack asks to be chief, and the boys choose Ralph. Why do they vote for Ralph and not for Jack?
Your answer
Professor Lovelore
Last question. Jack raises his knife over the trapped piglet, and the blade does not come down. Why not?
Your answer
Professor Lovelore

Good. Here is the word for the day.

Symbol: an object that stands for an idea. The conch is only a shell, but it calls the meeting and marks the chief. So far, it stands for civilization, from the Latin civis, a citizen.

Copywork model

Copied: “Ralph grasped the idea and hit the shell with air from his diaphragm. Immediately the thing sounded.” (Chapter 1)

One mark: The short second sentence ends in a full stop right after “sounded,” so the sentence stops as suddenly as the first blast of the shell.

Find the conch passage in your own copy. Copy two or three sentences of it exactly, punctuation and all.
In one sentence, say what one punctuation mark in your sentences does.
Show a starter

The ___ after ___ makes the sentence…

🧠 Memory passage

From “Ralph grasped the idea and hit the shell with air from his diaphragm.” to “the air over the island was full of bird-clamor and echoes ringing.”
